source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Explain why careful observations can guide further scientific exploration instead of ending with one answer.
node_labels: What counts as a scientific question or test

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Even careless observations provide dependable evidence for deciding what to investigate next.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Observations count as evidence only when they agree with our existing explanation.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Watching a puri puff in a kitchen cannot start scientific exploration; only laboratory observations can.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: An observation can open a new scientific question only if something visibly changes.

intelligence.enrichment: Scientific investigation is systematic and evolving: careful observations can answer one question while opening new questions and guiding further exploration. Observations produce evidence; evidence supports explanations and can lead to deeper questions. The learner explains that scientific investigation is systematic and evolving, so observations can support explanations and open further questions. Science is finished once the first answer is found, and everyday kitchen observations are not real scientific exploration.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Exploring the inquisitive mind. The student must decide: Explain why careful observations can guide further scientific exploration instead of ending with one answer. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. Recalculate the key; do not copy source.key. Every option must be a claim that could answer the stem, and wrong options must be the same kind of answer as the key (a next term, a named process, or a row of the same shape). If the stem continues a number list, every option names a next term. Never write that naming or writing a term is what creates the list. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason)
